quotes.text: The easy to build promise has become an impossible to govern reality. The model is broken because it's centered on the individual maker rather than the enterprise architecture.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core problem with maker-owned custom connectors.

quotes.text: You're creating a world where an employee leaves the company and three mission critical integration stopped working because the custom connector was tied to their identity or their personal environment.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete failure scenario every IT team recognizes.

quotes.text: We need to stop pretending that a browser-based designer is a professional development environment. In the power platform world, prototyping happens directly in the portal.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Challenges the habit of building production automation in the browser.

quotes.text: The 2026 strategy isn't about deleting power automate. It's about layering your architecture correctly. Think of power automate as your front end for automation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a balanced layering model instead of a tool war.

quotes.text: If your automation is not auditable at the transaction level, it is not enterprise-ready. You are building for a world where visibility is the only currency that matters.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear test for enterprise readiness of automation.

chapters.title: VNet integration as a governance mandate

takeaways: Custom connectors owned by individual makers create security gaps, maintenance work and hidden per-call costs at scale.
Logic Apps Standard runs custom connectors as built-in extensions in a VNet-integrated, single-tenant runtime with fixed hosting costs and infrastructure-as-code deployment.
Keep Power Automate for human-centric, team-level tasks and move mission-critical, cross-departmental integrations to Logic Apps Standard.
hook: Custom connectors in Power Automate feel like a quick win until they become ungoverned, costly and insecure. This episode shows integration architects and Power Platform admins why Logic Apps Standard, with VNet integration, Bicep deployments and fixed-cost hosting, is the better foundation for enterprise integrations and how to plan the migration.
